prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1500; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On arrival at the scene in Katy, Texas, I found a low-speed head-on collision between two passenger vehicles in the eastbound lane. Driver 1 stated that they were operating a vehicle with a Passenger seated beside them when Driver 2's vehicle crossed into their lane. Driver 1 reported pain in the lower back and said the impact had pushed them forward against the seatbelt. Driver 2 gave a statement that matched Driver 1's account of how the collision occurred. Two independent witnesses at the scene confirmed the sequence of events, and photographs taken at the scene are consistent with both statements. The Passenger and Driver 1 were both identified as occupants of the vehicle at the time of impact. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the insurance policy for that vehicle. Damage to the front of Driver 1's vehicle is consistent with this impact. A few older scratches were noted along the rear bumper, and it is not clear whether they were caused by this collision or existed before it. Further inspection will be needed to determine the extent of damage attributable to this incident.
